extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters) involved in inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive examiner guidance for conducting optional inter partes reexamination proceedings, including preparation/content of Office actions, timing, citations, appeals, and correspondence rules. Targets how examiners should evaluate patentability and manage the reexamination file and interactions with patent owners and third-party requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough prior art investigation and completeness of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention. The examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance of the application or patent under reexamination with the applicable statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as with respect to matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must investigate prior art and examine for statutory/rule compliance, patentability, and form matters. In appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects) the examiner's action may be limited to matters before further action; matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and explanation in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant, or in the case of a reexamination proceeding, both the patent owner and the requester, will be notified of the examiner’s action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant, or in the case of a reexamination proceeding the patent owner, to judge the propriety of continuing the prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions must state reasons for adverse actions, objections, or requirements and supply identifying references/information to help parties evaluate whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search availability
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared thereon at the time of the national examination on the merits, upon specific written request therefor and payment of the international-type search report fee set forth in § 1.21(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner/Office notes when international-type searches are performed and how request/fee operates; Office does not require such a formal report to obtain a search fee refund in a later-filed international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of claims when unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not considered patentable as claimed, the claims, or those considered unpatentable will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must reject unpatentable claims. Rejections should be explicit about which claims are rejected and on what grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing best references and explaining pertinence
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows or describes inventions other than that claimed by the applicant, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable. The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite patent numbers/dates/names (or publication numbers/dates/names for applications); identify specific pages/parts for foreign docs or printed publications; clearly explain how each reference pertains to each rejected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and examiner's personal-knowledge facts
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant, or the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, as to any matter affecting patentability and, insofar as rejections in applications are concerned, may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rejection is based on facts within an Office employee's personal knowledge, the data shall be as specific as possible and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee, subject to contradiction/explanation by applicant affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter qualifying as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f),(g) and joint research agreement rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter which is developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when subject matter is deemed commonly owned via joint research agreements (three-part test: agreement in effect on/before date invention made; invention result of activities within scope; application discloses or is amended to disclose parties). To overcome a 103 rejection based on such art, applicant must provide a statement that the parties were in a qualifying joint research agreement and the invention resulted from activities within its scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be stated when unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for allowance should be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or sent as a separate communication; the applicant/patent owner may file comments within a specified time. Failure to respond does not imply anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and mailing of first Office action with order
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action on the merits will ordinarily be mailed together with the order granting the reexamination. Where the order will be mailed without the first Office action, the order must indicate that an Office action will issue in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If first Office action cannot be mailed with the order, the Office action should be issued within two months from the mailing of the order, unless case awaiting merger, then within one month from mailing of the merger decision. Use form paragraph 26.04 to inform patent owner and requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of first action (ACP vs. rejection action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all of the patent claims are found patentable in the first action, the examiner will issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP). Where the examiner determines that one or more of the patent claims are to be rejected, the first Office action on the merits will be similar to a first action on the merits in an application (or ex parte reexamination) where a rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when following application-style format, inter partes reexamination practice must be followed: use inter partes forms, set special time periods, use inter partes form paragraphs, and send copies to both patent owner and third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content standard for first Office action (establish issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action will be a statement of the examiner’s position, and it should be sufficiently complete so that the second Office action can be an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP). It is intended that the first Office action be the primary action to establish the issues which exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action should be comprehensive and address all prior art patents/printed publications; set forth each ground of rejection/objection and the supporting reasons; specify determinations favorable to patentability and reasons for refusing to adopt requester-proposed rejections; respond to each argument in the request under 37 CFR 1.915. If incorporating a claim chart, carefully review to ensure incorporated items clearly and completely address patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting requester-proposed rejections to preserve appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should not refuse to adopt a rejection properly proposed by the requester as being cumulative to other rejections applied. Rather, any such proposed rejection must be adopted to preserve parties’ appeal rights as to such proposed rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if cumulative, adopt proposed rejections so parties retain appeal rights; if refusing to adopt, clearly state reasons for each refused proposed rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 35 U.S.C. 112 issues in first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, there will be no patent owner amendment to address in the first Office action of the inter partes reexamination, because 37 CFR 1.939(b) prohibits a patent owner amendment prior to first Office action. Thus, the first Office action will ordinarily contain no rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 112; a rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 112 is proper in reexamination only when it is raised by an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if a newly requested and granted reexamination is merged with an existing reexamination proceeding which already contains an amendment, then 112 issues raised by the amendment and any improper broadening under 35 U.S.C. 314 should be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about ACP and strict enforcement of amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the requirement for “special dispatch” in inter partes reexamination proceedings (35 U.S.C. 314(c)), it is intended that the examiner will issue an ACP at the earliest possible time. Accordingly, the first action should include a statement cautioning the patent owner that a complete response should be made to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First action should caution patent owner that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP and that any amendment after the ACP must include 'a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented'. Insert form paragraph 26.05 followed by form paragraph 26.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form and signature on first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the first Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office action cover sheet is PTOL-2064; where the Office action is a first Office action, the space on the PTOL-2064 for the date of the communication to which the Office action is responsive should not be filled in (order responds to the request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference and conferee initialing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a patent owner response to the action and third party requester comments where permitted by the CRU, or upon the expiration of the time to submit same, the examiner will be internally notified. The examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference pursuant to MPEP § 2671.03, to discuss the issuance of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with the two or more other conferees initialing the action (as 'conferee') to indicate their presence in the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation and review of requester materials (claim charts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the request for reexamination includes material such as a claim chart to explain a proposed rejection ... the examiner may bodily incorporate the claim chart (or other matter) within the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must carefully review any incorporated claim chart or material to ensure that items incorporated in a statement of the rejection clearly and completely address the patentability of the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title change procedure during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, the title of the patent will not need to be changed during reexamination. In those very rare instances where a change of the title does become necessary, the examiner should point out the need for the change as early as possible in the prosecution, as a part of an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change in title can only be effected via a formal examiner’s amendment accompanying the Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) at termination of prosecution. Patent owner may comment on the change, but final decision is the examiner’s and not subject to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim handling when base claims canceled or amended
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unamended base patent claim (i.e., a claim appearing in the patent) has been rejected or canceled, any claim undergoing reexamination which is directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be indicated as patentable if it is otherwise patentable. The dependent claim should not be objected to nor rejected merely because it depends upon a rejected or canceled original patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement for rewriting the dependent claim in independent form. If a new base claim has been canceled in reexamination, a claim which depends thereon should be rejected as indefinite. If an amended base patent claim or a new base claim is rejected, a claim dependent thereon should be objected to if it is otherwise patentable, and a requirement should be made for rewriting the dependent claim in independent form as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement for inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIAL DISPATCH.— Unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause, all inter partes reexamination proceedings under this section, including any appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reexamination proceedings will be 'special' throughout pendency. First Office action should ordinarily be mailed with the order. Cases involved in litigation have priority over other cases; reexaminations not in litigation have priority over other cases except those in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for responses, comments, appeals, and briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods for response and comments for the various stages of an inter partes reexamination proceeding are as follows: (A) After a non-ACP Office action: patent owner may file a response normally within two (2) months; requester may once file comments within 30 days of service. (B) After an Office letter indicating response not proper: complete within time set (normally 30 days or one month). (C) After an ACP: patent owner may once file written comments and/or proposed amendment normally within 30 days or one month; requester may once file comments within 30 days of service. (D)-(J) Detailed times for appeals, notices of appeal/cross-appeal, briefs, oral hearing requests, and appeals to the Federal Circuit; many times are non-extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific non-extendable times: notice of appeal within 30 days or one month (whichever longer); cross-appeal within 14 days of service of other party's notice; appellant brief and fee within two months after last-filed notice of appeal; respondent brief within one month of service; times for briefs and other filings often may not be extended. See cited CFR sections (e.g., 37 CFR 1.951, 1.953, 41.66, 41.61, 41.73, 1.304).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and correspondence methods and timeliness rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence relating to this inter partes reexamination proceeding should be directed: By EFS-Web (registered users), By Mail to Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam, By FAX to Central Reexamination Unit, By hand to Customer Service Window. For EFS-Web transmissions, 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(C) and (ii) states correspondence will be considered timely filed if transmitted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4) and includes a certificate of transmission stating the date of transmission prior to expiration of set period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include certificate of transmission for each piece of correspondence for EFS-Web filings; only certain filings (requests for reexamination and corrected/replacement requests) are exceptions. Inquiries regarding status should be directed to Central Reexamination Unit telephone number provided. Examiner note: parties are not to contact the examiner directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing of Office actions and copies to requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: After an Office action is completed and processed and has been approved by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) or Technology Center (TC) Quality Assurance Specialist (QAS), the action is mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes reexamination forms structured to print reexamination identifying info and correspondence address of patent owner. All actions will have a copy mailed to the third party requester using transmittal form PTOL-2070. If multiple requesters or owners, Office may treat first-named party's mailing address as correspondence address. Copies of Office actions may be obtained via Public PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time in an inter partes reexamination proceeding are governed by 37 CFR 1.956. It should be noted that extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.956 are not available to the third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to waive time provisions (e.g., to obtain an extension not otherwise permitted) can be attempted only by filing a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee) to waive the time provisions of 37 CFR 1.927. See MPEP § 2665 for details on patent owner extensions of time.
